plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom in the protea family, with a flower head up to 30 cm across. A crown of silky, pink-tipped bracts surrounds a center of creamy, feathery florets. It stands out against the leathery green leaves of the fynbos shrubland.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, mainly June to October
plants.location: Western Cape fynbos, South Africa, including the slopes around Cape Town and Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to an ancient plant family that dates back to when the southern continents were joined. Its thick underground stems help it survive the wildfires that regularly sweep the fynbos.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A garden favorite with big, ruffled, fragrant blooms in lush pink shades. They open above glossy, deeply divided leaves. Late-season varieties such as 'Sarah Bernhardt' carry the show into early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere, typically May to June
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the central United States, such as St. Louis, Missouri. The species is native to China and Siberia.
plants.funFact: Peonies are long-lived perennials. A single clump can bloom year after year for decades with little care. Ants often crawl over the flower buds to feed on the sweet nectar on their surface.
